land.text: the Kazakh SSR, 'detached from the Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic (RSFSR) and made the Kazakh Soviet Socialist Republic, a full union republic of the USSR' on 5 December 1936

predecessors.note: Kazakhstan 'proclaimed full independence on 16 December 1991, becoming the last Soviet republic to do so'; the USSR dissolved ten days later (page, no date given). Cliopatria's row starts in 1992.

capitals.name: Astana (Nur-Sultan 2019-2022)
capitals.note: 'On 10 December 1997, Kazakhstan's government relocated its capital from Almaty'; infobox Astana 51°8'N 71°26'E. Renamed Nur-Sultan in 2019 (Tokayev's 'first official act') and 'In September 2022, the capital's name was reverted to Astana'.

correction.text: the Kazakh SSR's territory, independent from 16 December 1991

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Kazakhstan 'proclaimed full independence on 16 December 1991' (sovereignty within the USSR on 25 October 1990), a year before Cliopatria's row begins. The 1992 outline is used for 1991. Cliopatria's USSR row also covers 1991, so the year is drawn by both dossiers; the rendering decides between the declared and the dissolved Union (26 December 1991).

2,641,282 km2 against the infobox 2,724,910 km2 (ratio 0.97, 'with an area of 2,700,000 square kilometres' in the text). The shape includes the 20 grid cells of the Baikonur lease (Natural Earth lists 'Baykonur Cosmodrome' as a separate unit): 'Russia, as the official successor state to the Soviet Union, has retained control over the facility since 1991' (Baikonur page), under a lease extended to 2050 (ratified by Russia on 8 June 2005); sovereignty is Kazakhstan's, so no event moves the land.

2,642,254 km2 (+972 km2 on 1992). The grid cells that differ (1 out, 5 in, at 44.7-46.7N 59.6-61.0E) lie on the Kazakh-Uzbek frontier where it 'cuts through the Aral Sea' along a 128 km straight segment, and the sea 'was formerly much larger but was severely depleted by Soviet-era irrigation schemes': a shoreline artefact, not a border move. The China agreements (26 April 1994, ratified 15 June 1995; 24 September 1997 and 4 July 1998 additions; protocol of 10 May 2002) moved at most a strip east of Lake Zhalanashkol, below one grid cell.

2,642,741 km2 (+488 km2). Again 2 cells out and 2 in at 44.7-45.5N 59.9-60.4E, the Aral Sea margin of the Uzbek frontier. The Russia treaty approved on 18 January 2005 'entered into force on 12 January 2006' but follows the former Kazakh-Russian administrative line, so it moved no land; the Uzbek treaties took effect on 5 September 2003 (Kazakhstan-Uzbekistan page).
Same outline as 2006-2023 (2,642,741 km2). January 2022 unrest ('large-scale protests following a sharp rise in fuel prices') did not touch the frontier.

region.text: the Kazakh SSR within its Soviet-era borders, capital Almaty

ledger.note: 16 December 1991: Kazakhstan proclaims independence, the last Soviet republic to do so. 'Kazakhstan declared its sovereignty within the Soviet Union on 25 October 1990' and 'proclaimed full independence on 16 December 1991'; 'Ten days after Kazakhstan's declaration, the Soviet Union itself dissolved.'

10 December 1997: the capital moves from Almaty to Astana. 'On 10 December 1997, Kazakhstan's government relocated its capital from Almaty.' Renamed Nur-Sultan in 2019 and Astana again in September 2022.

region.text: 'a narrow strip of hilly terrain east of Lake Zhalanashkol'

ledger.note: 2002: the border with China is finalised. 'finalized with the Protocol signed in Beijing on May 10, 2002'; 'a narrow strip of hilly terrain east of Lake Zhalanashkol' contested in 1969 'has become recognized as part of China'. The page does not say which agreement (1994, 1997, 1998 or 2002) gave the strip, so the year is the final protocol's; no area is given and the strip is far below one grid cell.

region.text: the Bagys area, 517 hectares of mountainous pastures

ledger.note: 2002: the Bagys dispute with Uzbekistan ends. 'Ultimately, Bagys was integrated into Kazakhstan'; 'An exchange of 517 hectares of mountainous pastures in the Bagys area' was made 'for semi-desert land in the Kyzylorda Region'. The treaty of 16 November 2001 defined 96% of the border and 'the Treaty on Specific Border Sections, signed on September 9, 2002' completed it (in force 5 September 2003). The page does not date the exchange; it is under 6 km2 and the Kyzylorda land given in return is not located.

certainty.note: The frontier is the Soviet administrative line (the Russian border 'became an international frontier in 1991' and was fixed by the treaty in force 12 January 2006), the China treaties of 1994-2002 and the Uzbek treaties of 2001-2002 (in force 2003; ratified again 28 March 2023). The Uzbek frontier across the Aral Sea is a 128 km straight line and the shoreline there is the only soft edge.

notes: Five pages opened (the budget). The four Cliopatria shapes are one outline: the area grows by 972 km2 in 1996 and 488 km2 in 2006 through 6 and 4 grid cells at the Kazakh-Uzbek frontier in the Aral Sea (44.7-46.7N, 59.6-61.0E), which is a shoreline effect of the shrinking sea, not a border treaty; all of the real treaties (China 1994-2002, Uzbekistan 2001-2003, Russia 2005-2006) moved less than one grid cell of land. The Baikonur lease is not an event: sovereignty stayed Kazakh, and the schema has no lease type; the 20 grid cells of the lease are inside the Kazakhstan shape. A renderer wanting the Russian presence could tint them as a client area. The Zhalanashkol loss and the Bagys gain are confidence 1 because the pages do not date the transfers; the gazetteer lacks 'Zhalanashkol' and 'Bagys'. The pages give no area for the China strip and none for the Uzbek exchange beyond the 517 hectares. Start 1991 (not 1992 as in Cliopatria): the declaration of 16 December 1991; 1991 is drawn with a new keyframe on the 1992 outline and overlaps the Soviet Union's last year. No war moved the border since 1991, so wars is empty.
